title: Binary Tree Right Side View
description: Return the rightmost visible node value at each depth, from top to bottom.
note: Visit each level from left to right and keep the value of its last node.
notes: The queue starts with the present root. Each node's left child is enqueued before its right child, so the last node removed from a level is that level's rightmost node.
repeat pending.size evaluates the count once before processing the level. Children added during its body wait for the next outer iteration, matching Python's range(len(pending)).

node is a function-local TreeNode even though its first assignment is inside repeat. The nonempty queue ensures at least one assignment on each outer iteration before res.push(node.val). A read with no prior assignment would raise a runtime initialization error; uninitialized state is distinct from none and does not change the static type.
Explicit presence checks preserve nodes whose value is zero. A deeper level can be visible entirely from the left subtree when the right subtree ends earlier.
LeetCode supplies TreeNode. The record declaration shows how the same type would be defined in a standalone Birdie program.
The traversal takes O(n) time and O(w) auxiliary queue space, where w is the maximum level width, plus O(h) result space for h levels. It does not modify the tree.
